verdict.tagline: Brutal combat and deep atmosphere trapped behind rough technical performance.
for_you_if: you want cooperative horde shooting with melee focus
not_for_you_if: you need a solo mode or offline play
you require stable frame rates without performance stutters
you want to avoid aggressive microtransactions

distortion_flags.sentence: Reviews shift dramatically from severe technical frustration in early hours to praise for core combat mechanics in later play.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks a solo mode or offline play, requiring a full group of four players to start matches even in private lobbies.

citations.review_text: For a game I'm sure its fun and worth the price when its on sale but for a game to not allow you to play in a solo lobby is insane to me. its something this game and Back 4 blood didn't understand that valve did when making Left 4 Dead

This game forces you to dive right into the unwashed masses and hope for the best. And no, I'm not just talking about the poxwalkers. There is no way to play this game singleplayer with bots. Instead, you must join up with other random players. This means your experience with this title is directly dependent upon the number of functioning braincells split between your team of four, divided by two of course because at least half of your fireteam will be low-functioning servitors who have, remarkably, not swallowed their own tongues...yet.

Until I can play by myself like the asocial, rock-dwelling hermit I am, I ain't going back to Tertium.
Not Solo - needs 4 people for pve
3 years after launch, still no solo mode

The game itself has potential, but the inability to play Solo is unnecessarily restrictive. Private lobbies still require four players before a match can begin, meaning that even players who simply want to practice, explore, or enjoy the game on their own are unable to do so.

Applying the same restriction to private lobbies defeats much of their purpose. Players should have the option to start a private match alone or with fewer than four people, even if the game is not specifically balanced around solo play but forcing a four-player requirement creates an unnecessary barrier to accessing the game. The lack of a basic solo option make it not even worth keeping this game.

citations.review_text: Optimisation has once again left the chat. Unfortunately, I didn't buy it from Steam so I can't refund, but this game runs like absolute garbage.

claims.claim: Reviewers note optimization issues and heavy frame rate drops, requiring graphical setting adjustments or workarounds to run smoothly.

citations.review_text: The setting is very interesting and the gameplay is fun. I had to use dlss to have a smooth experience in my system but was playable in the medium quality.

The game is okay gameplay-wise, but for a space L4D2 game it has GLARING optimization problems.
RTX with DLSS will drop your frames to about 40-30 fps or so, turning it off brought my frames back to a 80-ish. I actually recommend enabling fake frames because even on highest texture settings textures are pixelated, and DLSS amends that.
The worst part is that the pre-recorded cutscenes LAG, which is unacceptable. (How the f@#$ were they able to lag an MP4 decoder in my gpu?). Add to the fact that this game has framedrops in lobby, and you get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that runs worse than Vermintide.
Otherwise the game would be pretty fun, even with the MTX bull crap.

I bought this a few years ago and it did not run well at all for me. It tanked to 10-30 FPS max. It seems like the game has been worked on a bit and optimized. I can run it around 90-110 now as long as I disable raytracing. I enjoy the game quite a bit. I'm super new so far but I think it's a good game to pick up right now.

I'm very new to Warhammer 40k, alot of my friends are really into it so I wanted to give it a try through this game! 
From the 10 hours that I have played so far in this review, the game is really fun and I am slowly (VERY slowly) understanding more of the lore of what's happening in this game specifically. It also helps that my friends are super smart with Warhammer lore so I can always ask lol.

The community has also been very kind with a noobie like me.

The optimization for the game is probably my only issue, there's definitely a ton of options you need to tweak, but after troubleshooting the game runs smooth and looks super cool :3
pretty good! runs badly though. reduce resolution

The core idea of ​​the game is cool! There are also some details I really like—for instance, the way the firearms feel so impactful. Like having to slap the magazine in to seat it properly, or pulling the cocking handle back hard to chamber a round, and so on.

But it lacks a fair bit of polish. Especially when the game is almost 4 years old. For one thing, the frame rate fluctuates wildly. My hardware far exceeds the recommended system requirements, yet the FPS often drops to just above 30. And that’s while playing at 1080p on "High" settings with a 60Hz monitor—nothing too demanding compared to someone running 4K at 144Hz, for example. There's still stuff to complain about. But for what? Will the devs change it? Propably not...

But we know how it goes. As long as we players just buy the license of the games and the developers already have the cash in the bank, they don't really have to put in much effort...

claims.claim: Reviewers describe performance issues specifically on AMD systems, such as stuttering or requiring disabled Smart Access Memory or AI-generated frames.

citations.review_text: The game just isn't playable on AMD systems without disabling Smart Access Memory in your BIOS. This issue has been known about for years and years but nothing has been done to address it or even acknowledge it. The developers continue to put out content updates while ignoring a game breaking issue that affects a significant portion of the community, forcing them to choose between this game being unplayable or taking a performance hit on every single other game installed on their computer.
The game stutters on the best AMD GPU available. Works fine with driver enabled AI generated frames. No Ray Tracing enabled.

I'm still new to this game, about 15 hours in playing Psyker, and I'm already hooked. The combat feels great, both melee and ranged, and the 40k atmosphere is spot on. There's a lot to learn (weapons, perks, talents, crafting) so it can be a bit overwhelming at first, but once things start clicking it gets really rewarding. If you liked Vermintide or Left 4 Dead style co-op games, you'll probably like this one too.
Dustyhourglass on yt convinced me to play this game and I am glad. cool atmosphere and satisfying gameplay.
Very fun, fast and atmospheric...

This game had a rough start.  I played it back at launch, and it was nothing but bones.  Excellent bones, but bones all the same.  They have spent the last year somehow managing to not only continue working on content for their other title (Vermintide2), but also adding to, expanding, polishing, and all-'round improving this one.  

This game now feels complete:  combat is satisfying, the visuals and audio design are excellent (though visuals aren't without their occasional quirks), the classes are all distinct and interesting, the soundtrack ~*slaps*~, and there are piles of progression hooks for you prog nerds out there!

I'm super glad this game seems to have found it's footing.  If you love Warhammer, or are just curious about it, and you want a fun romp with 3 of your friends with a banger OST, this is your game! :)

Got it during summer sale, base game only. I've played 4 hours so I'm like halfway through the multiplayer training campaign, playing as a psyker. 

It's basically your typical L4D type zombie fighting game except you're a penal soldier in W40K fighting nurgle zombies in the underhive. So there are ogryns, psykers, tech priests, etc. The enemy variety is decent but anyone whose played these games before will recognize the chaff/elite/shooty/fast/boss categories the enemies fit into. 

There's a huge crafting/advancement system but the game does a good job of trickling lots of early advancement to you before the grind sets in. Also, playing in games with people who are thousands of hours ahead of you isn't completely terrible. 

The voice acting and plot (what little there is of one) is entertaining. It's an above average W40K game, as these things go. 

As of 2026, the game still has active players in the matchmaker.

Where did this game come from?  I remember play 1.0 at launch and being very unimpressed...  Like most Warhammer games, all looks and no substance...  reskinned Vermintide..
NOT THE CURRENT CASE:  The stuck with it and put in the work to 'find the fun' and really differentiate themselves from the other titles!  The heart of the formula is there, but really stuck to the tuning and cooking.
- Classes feel very different: the tempo, kit, different fantasies, flexible upgrade system
- The tile sets for the different maps are varies and wild...  factory, slums, gore halls, battle train, outside war outpost, ect.
- The flow of a left 4 dead/Vermintide, but stands on it's own with TONS of wh4k flavor and unique systems
- MORE MODES of play!  A roguelite mode, challenges and modifiers to maps...
If you find this on a discount, grab it...  Recommend the added classes as they all feel different and change things up.

I will keep this simple.  Admittedly I got this game on sale, right before the Skittari DLC dropped, because I play....or used to before 8th ed, play Adeptus Mechanicus in the tabletop game.  

If I had paid full price for this game, I would be quite frustrated.

Darktide is a party game, and that's about it.  If you have a group of friends, and just want to mess around, then I'm sure this has the same kind of appeal as Left 4 Dead did.

But let's be clear.  Replayability of this game is laughably low, and the skills tree is meaningless sweatmaxxing at its worst.  90% of the skill tree are things like "Gain +2% confidence in your life choices when you hit an Elite enemy while dodging sideways on a summer sunday." or "Teammates within 4m gain extra Cheerios when you have a Rule34 tab open while playing."

Jokes aside, it really is like MMORPG level stuff.  For the Skittari as an example, there are.....two abilities that actually change how you play, and they don't change much.  You can have your servo skulls, which include a flamethrower variant that barely does any damage, a servo skull that can revive teammates, and your basic one with a las pistol.  Then you can get arc grenades.....but you can't have them and the upgraded servo skulls at the same time......wtf?!

Other than that, the entire skill tree is just incremental enhancements to your health, stamina, armor, regen, damage, etc.  On top of this, most of the weapons in the game are insanely boring.  In the very beginning I was having fun, and that lasted about 20 mins.  Because its just mashing the same button over and over.  There is a "system" of blocks and counters and things, that will almost never be relevant because you don't have time to duel anything when you are being swarmed by enemies.  

This game has a ton of potential, but its totally wasted.  I do really like certain aspects.  I like the interactions between characters, it adds some personality and makes it feel engaging.  But the gameplay its…

This game is beautiful gem of art and gameplay design mastery.

This beautiful gem is buried deep in a dumpster someone doused in gasoline before setting it on fire, and somehow, nearly 4 years later, the fire is still burning and nobody came to pick up the trash. By that I mean that the game is forced online only (no possible solo play with or without bots, despite promises of the contrary before release), missions take roughly 25m, there are no checkpoints whatsoever and the game still crashes all the damn time. The latest DLC class is less an actual class and more of a bipedal collection of bugs so vast it might as well be a Hollow Knight collab... coincidentally at nearly the same price as Hollow Knight.

Still, if you are even remotely interested in horde shooters or WH40K's aesthetic, it's very hard to pass up.

citations.review_text:
Very nice 1st person team shooter game. Punishing, but fair. Good gameplay.

It is the same stuff every time. Play this game for 10 hours and you have basically seen it all. They keep adding new classes and that's nice, but I do not want to play through the same repetitive missions with a new character, I want to play new stuff. Do that. Add more missions, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, not more crap for me to pay too much money for. Add more content. Microtransaction shiny bolter chain whatever gun that's not content, that's just you trying to scam people. Shove it. Add more missions. 

The DLCs are nice but way too expensive. No, I am not gonna pay 20 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ euro for one class. That's what an entire video game should cost. Piss off. But otherwise yeah, the game is really good. I am just waiting for them to add more content, because the gameplay is really really nice.

TLDR: Meh. It's ok but Vermintide 2 is the better game. Lot of that will just come down to preference I guess. If you're a huge 40k or sci-fi fan and hate fantasy maybe you'll prefer this.

To me, this game is kind of meh. It's got that great Tide feel for sure, but everything else about it just doesn't quite hit. First up, it suffers from the same sort of thing a lot of games the past few years have suffered from: that is there is a certain fear that the player must be always engaged and never without action for even a fraction of a second. Battlefield 6 suffered from this as well. But games are better when you have time to slow down from time to time and catch your breath, contemplate your next action, etc. In Darktide, though you don't ever really clear all the enemies. You just drag them with you to the next encounter. This kind of makes things like the AI director sort of redundant: it seems like you're basically constantly fighting off the horde, massive amounts of specials, etc. So much so that it all kind of just blurs together with the main solution being just hack your way through it. The tactical level here is just poor.

Additionally I find the game dull to look at. I guess if you love the whole "grim-dark" thing you're going to love it, but to me it just looks like endless corridors of metal. There's very little variety on offer here as far as visuals: I can't tell one map from the next. And the narrative is confusing and dumb. In Vermintide 2 you were heroes! Here you're not even a cog in the machine of war. You're a spoke on a cog. Helldivers 2 already did the same thing but at least it was funny. Darktide is just depressing.

Darktide does get a few things better than VT2. The new player experience is significantly better. The itemization is generally better (less RNG, but the excitement of VT2's system is gone). The talent trees in Darktide are truly fantastic though - chef's kiss.

I don't hate Darktide. I'll probably continue to play it some, but …

Now I started my warhammer journey with vermintide and played it a lot with my friends so ill be comparing darktide with it.

Cons:
I found the melee of vermintide to be much responsive, darktide's melee seems 'laggier' than the other game. The animations for ability/weapon switching get stuck when the animation is already running? It makes the game feel less responsive.
 The central 'hub' is alright but quite useless, vermintide was focused with its lobby area.
 I don't really like the mission select terminal, the events are alright but they are lacking in variety. If you play a few of the events you've played them all. 
Forcing the players to play the starting levels and 7/8 levels to unlock certain shops or even the armoury is bad. I am incentivised to NOT switch characters due to this.
DLC classes are much more interesting and offer better gameplay in my opinon than Veteran/Ogryn classes.
The characters yapping before starting a mission during the loading screen simply annoyed me. Vermintide's 'cutscenes' were better however short they were.
Why is the per player kill count removed from this game? I had to use mods to see the scoreboard.

Pros:
Gorgeous environment, the banter is decent between characters, sometime repetitive but alright. 
Campaign is good.
Talent tree is interesting.

Mid:
Classes are good, i started with psycher, and its quite fun, juggling all the abilities in the heat of the combat and knowing which ones to use is quite fun.
Zealot is an okay class.
Higher difficulties unlock after a really really long time.
XP Gain is slow on higher levels, I would rather make my character overkill and move to other chars and level them up instead of grinding on old levels with my main character.
Mods support exists but the since the mods aren't allowed to edit the game files too much, the mods are simpler as compared to vermintide. And as such there is no 4+ or 8+ player mod, I have to play with a subset of my friends :(

Still if yo…
if you like warhammer GET this game!!! it is rlly fun and very good but there is limited missions and the rest or just shorter mission, But overall very good.

The game is amazing. Gunplay is good, classes are varied, killing chaos is fun. It's a good 40k game at its core. With that said, I can't recommend the game based on the direction the devs are taking it, in terms of additional content. While the main game stays stagnant in terms missions and story content/progression, they have pushed out three class DLCs. I feel the game is focusing on the wrong things. Fill out the core game first before moving on to additional characters. I also dislike the fact that they are charging for additional characters. While the game was not priced as a full triple A game and I have no issues whatsoever with cosmetic packs, I feel like I'm being nickel and dimed for additional content that affects gameplay. You should grab the base game if it's on sale. Hours of fun to be had.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features online-only play with no solo mode available.

citations.review_text: They have still not released a solo mode.  modders created a way to do it within months that they screwed up with updates. vermin tide had the ability to solo with bots. maybe if they put half the resources into the game that they use for cosmetics it would have already been released.

This game is beautiful gem of art and gameplay design mastery.

This beautiful gem is buried deep in a dumpster someone doused in gasoline before setting it on fire, and somehow, nearly 4 years later, the fire is still burning and nobody came to pick up the trash. By that I mean that the game is forced online only (no possible solo play with or without bots, despite promises of the contrary before release), missions take roughly 25m, there are no checkpoints whatsoever and the game still crashes all the damn time. citations.review_text:
Darktide is ok with the gameplay loop but it lacks the classic vermintide 2 charm, perhaps in the future darktide will be fully fleshed out.

The game still suffers from a memory leak issue and if you have a high refresh rate monitor the max fps cap is 120 for vsync. If fatshark could fix the memory leak issue that would be great for game stability.

I still regret buying this game, overall. Even after years now, it still feels like a huge downgrade from vermintide. 

The perforance is still bad. There are still bugs, even new ones, making old missions impossible to complete at the very end, and of course, you lose all progress and rewards of the whole mission. Still crashes and network issues.
Balance is questionable, which huge spikes. 

Gear is still just boring - instead of working to get rare gear like in vermintide from missions, you just buy it from vendors, and then have static and deterministic ways to upgrade everything, but all the upgrades are also just small incremental number increases, there is nothing exciting, and you are unlikely to feel any upgrade at all. Now, it's not like I am a fan of RNG, but this game lacks any excitement for equipment and upgrades. 

Also let's not even mention how all cosmetic options are incredibly boring, the more expensive they are, the worse they even seem to get - this includes the huge amount of premium cosmetics you have to pay extra for. Bizarre, honestly, there is just nothing you could want here either.

With friends, of course, you can have some fun, the atmosphere of 40k is still great here, but I can't really say that I am ever having fun playing this game.

game runs so bad most times i actually pray to the omnissiah before launching

really fun though

Music, Atmosphere, gore. its all there.
Gameplay is repetative but when its this cool who tf cares.
Minor issues, poor optimisations, few non game breaking bugs. biggest problem is the monetisation but its not required.
A game I keep coming back to

4/10 ADD REAL CONTENT, characters dont equal content. barely any actual content to play through at all. this game is extremely boring and barely even runs even after 4 years. The game should be better by now and should be worth my time but it keeps becoming worse and worse. like yay new class added. no new maps, paywalled weapons ofc, oh and did I mention the game barely working as usual and everyone even in console struggling to have a proper play session without it having issues. from gameplay to story to what is under the hood, the requirement to run mods on the game to make it playable, there being input queues on everyone even though they are aware that when surrounded in a massive crowed you cant time your attacks or properly block the shots coming at you and keep meleeing while the game ♥♥♥♥♥ up all your inputs and you lose your train of thought and now you are just taking damage trying to figure out what your keybinds where because of the input delay and the weird preference for not focusing on fixing the fundamental issues with the game and preference over i dont know what exactly.

claims.claim: The game features cooperative horde shooter gameplay with combined melee and ranged combat mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Blessed be the cogitators. Blessed be the Tech-Priests who coded these long nights of purgation. Blessed be the servers of Fatshark, who in their toil for the Machine God have wrought something worthy of the name grimdark.

I have spent 1,143 hours in the underhive of Tertium upon the ash-choked world of Atoma, and I have not yet tired of the slaughter. That, by itself, is a miracle worth recording in the annals. Let this review stand as a hymn of praise — and, Emperor-willing, a thing of use to any Rejects still deciding whether to descend.

At first glance, this is a simple thing — a shooter, a game of trigger and blade. Heresy of a thought. Beneath the surface hums a machine of terrible complexity, classes each a cathedral unto itself, and within each class a dozen further heresies of build, loadout, and blessing to explore. I have played not one, but all, and still I find new catechisms to learn. The Omnissiah rewards those who study; the game punishes those who do not. This is as it should be.

The melee and ranged war-craft weave together in a manner few dare attempt — a hybrid liturgy of blade and bolt that looks, to the unschooled eye, like button-mashing chaos. It is not. Positioning, timing, the sacred rhythm of block and cleave and reload — these are disciplines, and the game teaches them slowly, cruelly, and fairly. Every death is a lesson from the Machine Spirit itself, and I have thanked it even as I bled out on the deck plating.

The atmosphere is a triumph of the Adeptus Mechanicus' own craft. Every corridor drips with grime and prayer-strips and the incense of promethium. Every limb parted from its heretical owner by shotgun-blast is rendered with a care that borders on reverent — as though the artists themselves were once executioners, and are pleased to remember the work.

And the sound! Omnissiah bless the sound engineers above all others. I no longer need eyes to know a beast has marked me for its own — the audio cue sings through the bone befor…

[b]This is one of the best 40K games and easily the best horde shooter around.[/b]

The action is very intense and mechanically rewarding, with both melee combat and gunplay being really fun. There are enough classes each with enough variety on their weapons and skills to allow for many distinct play styles. The skill ceiling is also high enough that good players can make anything work.

The community seems great for the most part too, especially the players that roleplay the Ogryn. In hundreds of hours of playtime I’ve only met a couple of players that seemed to think the game was meant to be played via complaining in chat instead of left clicking on enemies.

It also looks fantastic and the environments are very detailed. It looks especially good if you have the performance to spare to play with raytracing on (the performance hit is massive) even though the baked lighting looks fantastic too.
As a side note I feel like performance is inconsistent at times, even in similar situations in the same map, on occasion the game will seem to tank for no reason. It feels like a game restart can help sometimes but I’m unsure if it's a coincidence or it's just simply variations due to the way the enemy spawns work in this game.

Highly recommended!

a great horde shooter. excellent themeing, the classes feel unique, good gun play and masterful melee so deeply intertwined they are inseperable. the only down sides is sometimes there are so many dudes you cant tell why you died. it ends up being that you didnt pay attention to noise queues, every single time.

still dont know why the devs hate the veteran tho. hes literally just call of dooder man. just let him shoot things fatshark. thats his whole identity.

Was drawn in initially via their Previous Game Vermintide, that melee combat with gunplay has been shown to be a proper combination without the need to be focused on a particular "Meta" build to progress with each difficulty. 

Quite a large change and development over time since the BETA, many quality of life add-ons that arguably should've been there closer to the start.

However the gameplay loop was something that was held down well.

Though the cosmetic store is something to be desired (Unlike the catelogue option in previous titles, the cosmetics are 'rotated' out bi-weekly leaving a partial case a FOMO, and the usage of a "Currency" that will leave you with a partial amount left but never enough to get rid of.)

Big seller for me personally was the dialogue and characters, though initially coming in was a bit apprehensive that your personal character would be somewhat of a shell with your nametag on it. 
Thanklfully proven wrong with over 90,000 lines of dialogue for the different "personalities" which have their own underlying flaws and issues, and EXCELLENT line delivery from the voice actors! 

Only concern now is end-game, I did try not to bring up meta however It is to be said, that the balancing for the weapons and classes have been Buff heavy so every weapon that falls behind gets buffed, then the next one does, then the next, continue on for four years and now you have certain builds and weapons that completely over-shadow other weapons and DECIMATE higher armor classes. 

And now the developers are stuck in a conundrum, introduce even larger enemies groups, introduce changes that make the enemies tankier or more dangerous to engage in melee. Or players get bored.

Or dial it back, nerf the outliers that completely change the game, it still retains the horde managment with specials and heavy elite targets being a danger to the group, but now they don't immediately get bodied by certain weapons.

All in all Darktide is a game I find myself returning to…

[h2]Nota Geral | Overall Rating[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐

[b]Warhammer 40K: Darktide entrega um dos melhores combates corpo a corpo e à distância que já vi em um jogo cooperativo de hordas, mas peca gravemente numa área que deveria ser básica: dar suporte real pra quem quer jogar sozinho. O jogo permite jogar em sessão privada com bots preenchendo o esquadrão, só que na prática essa opção é quase decorativa, a IA dos bots é péssima e simplesmente não cumpre o papel de um jogador real. Isso empurra o jogador pra sempre depender de matchmaking online, o que não seria um problema se o próprio matchmaking não te punisse quando faltam jogadores de verdade, te jogando pra partidas cheias de bot de qualquer jeito.[/b]

[i]Warhammer 40K: Darktide delivers some of the best melee and ranged combat I've seen in a cooperative horde game, but it seriously falls short in an area that should be basic: giving real support to those who want to play solo. The game lets you play in a private session with bots filling out the squad, but in practice this option is almost decorative, the bot AI is terrible and simply doesn't fulfill the role of a real player. This pushes the player to always rely on online matchmaking, which wouldn't be a problem if the matchmaking itself didn't punish you when real players are missing, throwing you into matches full of bots anyway.[/i]

[h2]Jogabilidade | Gameplay[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]O combate é excepcional. O sistema de melee tem um peso e uma sensação tátil que poucos jogos do gênero conseguem replicar, cada golpe de espada ou machado sente como se realmente estivesse conectando com o inimigo, e a variedade de classes, cada uma com seu próprio estilo de jogo, dá camadas táticas reais pra composição de equipe. O problema não está na mecânica em si, que é sólida do começo ao fim, mas em como o jogo lida com a ausência de jogadores reais: se você cai em combate, raramente os bots vão te levantar, e se um bot cai junto com você, os outros dois praticamente não conse…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe specific enemy design complaints, noting that Poxbursters can be silent, buggy, or have inconsistent hitboxes, and that certain heavy enemies block visibility or lack audio cues.

citations.review_text:
put about 140 hours into the game as of this review and this game is great. melee combat feels good and is good. One problem I had with vermintide was (with certain weapons) the lack of impact they had. This game fixes that and makes each weapon feel like YOU are using it. Every character is powerful, some more so than others(psyker's existence), but every character in this game IS and WILL continue to be powerful. The game does a good job of making most of the enemies feel fair to fight. However, there are some complete blunders in terms of enemy design. 

Poxbursters: Buggy as hell. On paper, they're an enemy that makes sense in this game and when they work, they're fun. However, when the game either spams more than 2 of them at the same time or the game decides to not work, you are suddenly punished with 100 health damage and your toughness MISSING. Bugs may or may not include: not getting stunned by shoves, randomly exploding when they werent even touched, STILL not exploding after getting stunned by a shove rarely, completely silent sometimes, and can turn mid jump which looks weird. 

Bulwarks and crushers: Huge giant ass enemies that take up space so that other enemies can sneak ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hits on you sometimes. Its especially bad when you get a trapper thats behind 4 bulwarks and lets say 6 crushers. Theres no way of ever knowing that there was a trapper there without the audio cue. Not to mention crushers are dead silent most of the time and can just one shot you.  

Trappers: okay enemy but lag, visual and noise clutter among other things make trappers a complete nightmare to fight. Also has the same issue as a poxburster where multiple of them breaks the games balance and the AI director likes to spam these girls a lot. Also sometimes dead silent.

Vanguards: Pre-nerf vanguards WERE THE WORST. They were enemies that had 2000 hp, had 50% headshot resistance, had a shield that once broken, makes them unstaggerable. ontop of that, they'd spam these guys consta…

This game is a horrendous mix of a GENUINELY super fun and enjoyable game and the worst decisions possible. the gameplay, music and visuals are all amazing, with varied character builds. but then the game itself cant stop ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the bath at every turn. every update is like 2 steps forward and 5 back, with Fatshark not addressing major problems and glitch's which still are prevalent, such as certain enemies not making the sound to alert you to their presence, or a genuinely anti-player directory that spawns literally 60 of the same enemy in one room with little other variety. not to mention the other problems with enemy design, like carapace being seen as too strong, new shield enemies that look like normal enemies but with more health and armor than even the armored orgyns. or how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ poxbursters are with the aforementioned sound glitch, the hitbox being larger than their explosion, the aggro/stagger of them rubberbanding depending on who their currently running at, or their ridiculous damage. Fatshark doesnt ever seem to listen to feedback so I dont know. despite this games potential, and even ability to be super fun, every other moment with it is pure frustration to no end.

The problems with this game are numerous to be sure.
1. Expeditions is a shallow game mode that is a shadow of what chaos wastes was in Vermintide 2
2. The average player is so ridiculously bad at this game that playing with randoms almost always ends in a game over in any difficulty above heresy
3. Toughness is a crutch that emphasizes bad positioning and poor situational awareness
4. Mortis trial buff system should've been a part of expeditions
5. Cosmetics are overpriced
6. The difficulty cap system on new characters pads out game time in the worst way possible
7. Toxbursters and the new vanguard chaff are the 2 worst units in this game for different reasons. The toxburster hitbox is inconsistent and removes way to much health and at times the A.I director spawns an egregious amount. the new vanguard chaff does nothing but slow down the party as their health is overtuned to the point that you can kill crushers faster than these non-elite enemies.
8. There is no incentive to fight the daemonhost.
9. Melee weapons are so widely inconsistent in quality that 90% of them have no use on any class
10. Plasteel in general takes to long to acquire compared to diamintineand is used more than the "rare" material
11. Rolling weapons for the best stats is pure rng and shouldn't be part of the experience. In practice you should be able to customize your weapons stats to your liking.
12. The online hub is not only bland but also unnecessary peer-to-peer makes more sense
13. Map variety and atmosphere is lackluster
14. The voice acting lacks all character
15. No scoreboard without the use of mods
16. No actual incentive to collect grims
17.  Mission screen is random instead of allowing player freedom
18. Curios are not shared across characters and the slots are locked behind player progression
19. Packs of enemies will spawn directly in front of you instead of organically entering the environment
20. The "70+ weapons at launch" has still yet to be included
…

Honest and Harsh oppinion,

its a good game ruined by a bunch of very big problems. 

1. The community has its corners that is trying really hard to make the game in general a welcoming place but my personal experience has told me, if u decide to be the guy that is doing everyone in the party a solid and sag behid a bit to loot the materials and u just so happen to solo q AND MAYBE EVEN WORSE get into a  lobby with a 3 Stack, u will absolutly be kicked from the mission barring you from a majority of the EXP and MATS.

2. Even though FatShark has improved in the way they handle things a lot, i still think a lot of things are still not even remotly close to being in an acceptable state. Bugs, very questionable game design choices and and over all "we can fix it later down the line, ups cant anymore" attitute makes it really hard to look past all the problems this game has sometimes.

In general i would say YES IT CAN BE A LOT OF FUN (wouldnt have played over 400H by time of writing of not duh), just be warned that u r definitely not signing up for a flawless AAA, Loving community experience here. 

Not so Secret Tipp:
Bring Friends! Not having to suffer the tortures of soundles Poxbusters and Mouthbreathing teamm8s alone helps a lot!

Big seller for me personally was the dialogue and characters, though initially coming in was a bit apprehensive that your personal character would be somewhat of a shell with your nametag on it. 
Thanklfully proven wrong with over 90,000 lines of dialogue for the different "personalities" which have their own underlying flaws and issues, and EXCELLENT line delivery from the voice actors! 

Only concern now is end-game, I did try not to bring up meta however It is to be said, that the balancing for the weapons and classes have been Buff heavy so every weapon that falls behind gets buffed, then the next one does, then the next, continue on for four years and now you have certain builds and weapons that completely over-shadow other weapons and DECIMATE higher armor classes. 

And now the developers are stuck in a conundrum, introduce even larger enemies groups, introduce changes that make the enemies tankier or more dangerous to engage in melee. Or players get bored.

Or dial it back, nerf the outliers that completely change the game, it still retains the horde managment with specials and heavy elite targets being a danger to the group, but now they don't immediately get bodied by certain weapons.

All in all Darktide is a game I find myself returning to…

Darktide is a 10/10 game is disguised as a 7/10 by every other mechanic that isn't the core gameplay loop. I sometimes question if the developers know what they are doing, but the main combat loop, when you are actually pushed to utilize all the mechanics is so good it supersedes all the other issues I have with it. Plz fix cosmetic rotation and give the dlc classes more cosmetics massive megalodon I want to spend more money on this game.

I love this game, the skill floor to have fun and see all the missions isn't too high. You have to pay attention and know the basics, but you can get through all the missions without being some kind of full time gamer. On the other hand the skill ceiling is through the roof, there are so many cool mechanics and synergies to dig into that if you're a huge fan of build crafting you'll love the game
The DLC classes are a lot of fun, even if I think for most people they may not be worth it at full price. Each class is unique and brings something to the table, in fact more than one something, since there are so many build options that two veterans could fill completely different roles.
My only real complaint is that the microtransactions use a premium currency which cannot be gained in game outside of occasional community events, and even then only in nearly meaningless amounts. Further the microtransaction store has a dose of FOMO to drive purchases. I consider both FOMO and premium currency to be predatory. On the other hand other than the classes, all purchases beyond the base game are cosmetic only, so you won't be out shown by someone because they spent a fortune in the premium shop.

Get this game, especially if you have friends who want to play with you, or if you're a big Warhammer 40,000 nerd.

Go kill some heretics for the Omnissiah!

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the soundtrack, sound design, and Warhammer 40k atmosphere are standout features of the game.

citations.review_text: Only got into this game to play Skitarii. It used to run like poop when I bought it on release but seems to run a lot better now. I had a lot of fun, and it has a really good soundtrack. You'll definitely like this game if you like Vermintide, but I would recommend only picking it up on sale along with whatever class DLC peaks your interest because some of it is kind of overpriced. It wouldn't be Warhammer without Game Workshop's signature overpricing.

I'm a fan of Fatshark, the producers, and the "Tide" games (not the cleaning brand but instead Vermintide - 1 & 2 and Darktide). They know what their winning formula is: letting the player pretend they are John Wick as they dodge, duck, dive and dodge, all while slicing and shooting hordes of enemies. It is a hard game and you can always improve at it. That's the draw: the gameplay is fun, and you get to see those moments where you enter a totally "impossible" situation, and yet you pull victory out of the jaws of defeat. It isn't a series of quick-time events, it is you, the player, dodging, parrying, shooting, and slashing in the right time to dodge their strikes and deliver the fatal blows. It gives such a rush and a thrill, I haven't found in many other games. But because it is also hard, there will be more times where you get stomped flat and run over. But as you get better, it's really fun to turn those would-be failures into a clutch win. The dlc's are great and every aspect has a lot of effort and love put into it. The atmosphere is so immersive and awe inspiring. It has stability issues, especially when you use mods (which I recommend you do) and when they release new content that breaks the game in unexpected ways. But they are quick to fix most of them and they treat their players well as a company. 
10/10 would pet a chaos hound.
Nails the WH40k atmosphere perfectly. Soundtrack is a banger and the classes are all enjoyable to play with.

It's fun, it's a tide game, it's in a good spot after all the DLC classes.
If you've liked any of Fatshark's previous games you'll like this one, and if you've followed Fatshark you'll know the usual caveats to their games.

Darktide is no different but possibly the most polished and biggest in scope they've done so far.
Great use of the 40K license and great music as well, overall a slightly rough gem.
